outline.note: Stop 1. Fade in low on the reactor building; the camera rises into the low hero view, the plant right of centre. Then the presenters, the title in the dark sky, the QR.
Stop 2. The camera rises; the plant shrinks into a point on a filled ground while Lithuania opens around it: wind turns, solar shines, power flows to the cities. "50 %" counts up once.
Stop 3. A calm night: the turbines slow, the sun sets, local flows fade, imports grow; a controllable node lights up. "And when there is no wind or sun?"
Stop 4. Lithuania warms up: the country is assessing the BWRX-300 (memorandum, February 2026).

Stop 5. Down into the node: the plant grows back as the map closes; beside it, at the same scale, a large ESBWR-class plant rises (~1,500 MW vs ~300 MW). The two reactor vessels appear side by side at one scale: as tall, much wider. Then (automatically) the large plant steps back and four more BWRX-300 units are built one after another: 5 x 300 MW.
Four more BWRX-300 units assemble one after another behind ours: 5 x 300 MW. The large unit steps back.
Stop 6. The comparison falls away; one unit remains, its hall lit, its line carrying power out. "~300 MW" counts up once it reads, beside the line it leaves by.

Stop 7. From above, at one ground scale: the power block's ~148 x 78 m outline draws around our plant; beside it an international-size 105 x 68 m pitch in a schematic stadium (the National Stadium being built in Vilnius is a UEFA category 4 project: 105 x 68 m). "~1.6 football pitches of area" with its sources.

Stop 8. A second, identical unit goes up beside ours while a 0-36 month timeline fills; the 24-36 band lights and "24-36 months*" lands with its qualifier (vendor estimate, series unit, first nuclear concrete to fuel load). Illustrative: one unit's construction window, not two plants built together.

Stop 9. Up into geography: the plant becomes the Darlington pin as the North Atlantic opens; the other pins appear one by one, styled by status. Then (automatically) the camera glides to Canada: Darlington, under construction (CNSC licence April 2025); the other pins step back.
The camera glides to Canada: Darlington, under construction (CNSC licence April 2025); the other pins step back.

Stop 10. Into the Darlington pin: the plant grows out of it as the map closes, the camera arriving on the approved descent where it starts to push in; then (automatically, no exterior stop) the descent itself: ground, shaft, containment; the vessel opens on the core.
The approved Stage 3 descent from its push-in (master 1.5-15.4 s at 1.45x): ground, shaft, containment; the vessel opens on the core.

Stop 11. From a spot on the fuel the micro view opens: neutron -> U-235 -> split -> heat, three neutrons (one absorbed) -> two more splits -> a handful -> the view widens into a steady field of fissions in the fuel, held indefinitely (no restart).

Stop 12. The micro view collapses into the fuel spot as warmth (this happens in the fuel); then (automatically) out to the control blades, one illustrative insert / withdraw cycle, and a hold with both statements.
From the warm spot back out: the fuel, the bundles, then the control blades, copper; the reaction cue (glints) at full. The blades are the subject; the bright fuel stays a step back.
The blades move in; the glints thin out.
The blades move back out; the glints return. Both statements stay for the hold.

Stop 13. Reactor -> dry steam. The control demo settles; water rises through the core and boils; the mixture rises through the chimney; cooler water returns down the sides. Then (automatically) separators throw the water out, the dryer catches the last drops: dry steam leaves the vessel.
Separators throw the water out, the dryer catches the last drops: dry steam leaves the vessel.

Stop 14. Steam -> turbine -> condenser. Steam runs along the main steam line to the turbine; the shaft starts turning. Then (automatically) under the turbine the condenser turns exhaust steam back into water; pumps send it back to the reactor. The water cycle closes.
Under the turbine the condenser turns exhaust steam back into water; pumps send it back to the reactor. The water cycle closes.
Stop 15. Grid -> homes. The generator sends electricity out of the hall, through the transformer, along the line: the city lights up (scale illustration), "~300,000 homes*".
Stop 16. Normal -> power loss -> scram -> decay heat. Back from the city to the plant, still running; then (automatically) external power is lost, the reaction stops, but the heat remains; hold.
External power is lost: the line goes dark, the hall lights go out, the site dims, steam stops, the turbine winds down.
The chain reaction stops: every blade goes in, the glints die out.
But the heat does not go away: the vessel stays warm (decay heat). Fission ≈ 0, heat ≠ 0.

Stop 17. The isolation condenser loop: steam rises to the submerged condensers, heat goes into the pool, water returns by gravity. No pump. Then (automatically) time runs once: 0 h -> 7 days*, and stops; the passive loop keeps running; hold.
Time runs once: 0 h -> 1 day -> ... -> 7 days, then stops; the passive loop keeps running. One eye path: reactor -> loop -> the right column.

Stop 18. The rhythm slows: wide over the plant, calmly lit again. Three honest limits, each tied to a place: spent fuel in casks beside the reactor; licensing, layered approvals on the reactor building; first-of-a-kind risk, a schedule with an uncertain end, on the site.

Stop 19 (the last press). The limits text clears; vessel, containment, shaft and ground close while the camera glides through open space back to the opening view; the grid reconnects; then (automatically) the thesis, "Your questions" in amber, the presenters, the larger QR. Holds for Q&A.
The opening composition again (same low hero camera): the thesis at display size, "Your questions" in amber, the presenters, the larger QR. Holds for Q&A.
